findings.issue_text: Membership loading in both group routes uses fire-and-forget findMembers() calls instead of the awaited afterModel hook, allowing transitions to finish before data arrives and request failures to bypass route error handling, potentially leaving blank or stale member lists
admin-group totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, creating an extra empty page when the user count is an exact multiple of the page limit

The members endpoint defaults to 50 results, but the public group-members UI makes only one request and provides no pagination or load-more mechanism, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members
The admin group creation endpoint does not assign the alias_level sent by the client, so non-default values revert to the database default after reload
The automatic-group remove_member test uses PUT even though the route only accepts DELETE, so the controller spec bypasses routing and cannot detect HTTP verb or routing regressions

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The members endpoint defaults to 50 results, but the public group-members UI makes only one request and provides no pagination or load-more mechanism, silently truncating groups with more than 50 members

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for the public group-members route (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6), it calls model.findMembers() which makes a single request with default limit of 50. The template (group/members.hbs) iterates over 'members' but shows no pagination controls. The admin group UI has pagination (next/previous actions), but the public group members view does not. This means groups with more than 50 members will only show the first 50 without any way to see more members in the public view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The admin group creation endpoint does not assign the alias_level sent by the client, so non-default values revert to the database default after reload

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the create method in Admin::GroupsController, it only sets group.name and group.visible from params, but does not set group.alias_level. The update method does set alias_level: 'group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?'. This means when creating a new group, even if the client sends an alias_level parameter, it will be ignored and the group will be created with the default alias_level (0). This is a real bug - the create action is missing the alias_level assignment that exists in update.
